SAP HANA and HANA Cloud

Source: vignettes/hana.Rmd
hana.Rmd

Use oauth_db_hana() to query SAP HANA or SAP HANA Cloud with each visitor’s JWT access token. The helper returns a DBI connection; HANA validates the token and maps its external identity to a database user. That user’s database privileges determine the data they can query.

This guide covers SQL access to the HANA database. SAP BTP browser sign-in, SAP application APIs and the separate HANA Cloud data lake relational engine have their own setup.

Before running the app

Install odbc in R and a current SAP HANA Client with the HANA ODBC driver for your R architecture. Use odbc::odbcListDrivers() to find the installed driver name, commonly HDBODBC. On Unix, your driver manager may also accept the full path to libodbcHDB.so or the platform’s equivalent library.

Ask your database administrator for the SQL endpoint and JWT configuration:

Setting Where to find it
Server and SQL port HANA Cloud instance connection details, or your self-hosted HANA administrator; HANA Cloud normally uses port 443
Tenant database, if needed Self-hosted HANA connection details; usually omit it for a HANA Cloud endpoint
OAuth issuer Authorization server trusted by the database’s JWT provider
Client ID and secret Your OAuth application registration
Access scope and token audience Provider application configuration agreed with the HANA administrator
TLS trust store, if needed Certificate chain and trust-store format required by your SAP HANA Client TLS provider

Register an authorization-code client with PKCE at that OAuth provider. The local app’s redirect URI is http://localhost:8100. Configure the provider to issue JWT access tokens whose issuer, identity claims and audience match the HANA JWT provider. An ID token or an opaque access token does not substitute for the access token used by this helper.

The example below uses OIDC discovery. Enable refresh-token issuance at the provider when requesting offline_access, or use the provider’s documented refresh setup. There is no shared SAP scope or resource URL: database.read below is an example scope your administrator must define or replace. Configure any required audience in the provider’s application settings or its supported authorization parameters.

Save these values in your local .Renviron and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-shiny-app-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-shiny-app-client-secret
OAUTHDB_HANA_ISSUER=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
OAUTHDB_HANA_SCOPE=database.read
OAUTHDB_HANA_SERVER=your-instance.hana.prod-eu10.hanacloud.ondemand.com
OAUTHDB_HANA_PORT=443
OAUTHDB_HANA_DRIVER=HDBODBC

A complete app

This app displays the database user HANA assigned to the visitor. Replace the query with a table or view the signed-in user can read.

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

scope <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_SCOPE")
provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_ISSUER")
)
client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "offline_access", scope),
  required_scopes = scope
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_hana(
    auth$connection,
    server = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_SERVER"),
    port = as.integer(Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_PORT", "443")),
    driver = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_HANA_DRIVER", "HDBODBC"),
    required_scopes = scope
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER AS DATABASE_USER FROM DUMMY")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

Save the app as example.R and run source("example.R"). Open http://localhost:8100 in a regular browser; embedded IDE viewers cannot complete the OAuth redirects.

For a self-hosted tenant, set its SQL port and add database = "REPORTING" when required by the connection details. Use schema = "SALES" to select an initial schema. Set ssl_trust_store if the client’s configured trust store does not contain the server’s certificate chain. The helper always requires encryption, certificate validation and the endpoint’s hostname.

Configure HANA’s JWT provider

The target database needs a JWT provider, trusted signing certificates, external-identity mappings and grants for the mapped database users. Follow SAP’s JWT configuration procedure for HANA Platform, or the corresponding procedure for your HANA Cloud release. Configure the provider to check the intended issuer, signing keys and audience and to map the appropriate identity claim.

The Shiny client must obtain the token that this database configuration accepts. A successful SAP BTP or application-console login alone does not provide a HANA SQL identity. The helper does not create database users, grant privileges or configure certificate rotation.

SAP documents JWT login with an empty username and the token in the password field for both on-premise HANA and HANA Cloud. The helper uses that form and restricts the client’s authenticationMethods property to jwt; it does not use a saved database password, user-store key, session cookie or the host’s Kerberos account.

Connection lifetime and validation

Call connection <- con() before each operation. The helper reuses a valid SQL connection through ordinary token renewal. HANA continues to apply that database session’s identity and privileges; changing token claims does not change an already-open SQL session. Sign-out, account replacement, loss of required OAuth permissions and Shiny session end close the connection through DBI.

Native automatic reconnect is disabled. If a connection becomes invalid, the next con() opens a new one with a current token. Handle a failed query in your app; the helper does not replay it. A retained native handle is not a revocable authorization reference, so obtain the connection from con() rather than keeping it across operations.

Automated tests cover the real R ODBC connection-string boundary and use SQLite connections for session-lifecycle tests. Live SAP driver/server compatibility has not been verified. Before deploying, check CURRENT_USER for two visitors with different grants, a denied query, token renewal and reconnect, and the configured TLS certificate chain. Driver setup follows SAP’s HANA Cloud ODBC guide.
